threads.label: US strike posture and Qatari mediation
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post cited US officials saying a strike on Iran is a question of "when," with forces reportedly ready within 96 hours of a Trump order, while Trump said no strike would occur Sunday. Qatari mediators arrived in Tehran in a US-coordinated effort, as Iran International reported Trump weighing a deal versus further military action.

threads.label: Mecca Pact talks in Tehran
threads.summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan were set to meet Iranian counterparts in Tehran on Monday for talks on regional coordination, per Jerusalem Post and Iran International. IRIB reported Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir arrived in Tehran for a joint multilateral meeting with Iran's senior security official.

threads.label: Netanyahu-Zamir reported Iran split
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported that Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir clashed over military action against Iran days before Israel's elections. Defense Minister Israel Katz denied the reports and said Israel had no plans to strike Iran before the vote; Netanyahu adviser Ophir Falk called for Iran's regime removal.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes on Hamas commanders
threads.summary: The IDF announced the killing of Hamas intelligence officer Mohammed Halawa in a Saturday Gaza City strike and engineering officer Ahmed Zahir Fuad Abu-Odeh in a Thursday strike, citing ceasefire violations. The IDF also downed a drone near Kibbutz Nahal Oz and diverted a munition from a Gaza City strike after identifying uninvolved individuals.

threads.label: US naval posture in Gulf region
threads.summary: CENTCOM reported Adm. Brad Cooper visited the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday as part of US efforts to maintain shipping and crude oil flows, and posted imagery of an F-35C landing on USS George Washington operating in the Arabian Sea. Defa Press claimed deployment of an RC-135U Combat Sent surveillance aircraft at Al Udeid base in Qatar.

threads.label: US Treasury sanctions and Iran oil evasion
threads.summary: The Federal Register published an OFAC SDN List notice and a proposed Outbound Investment Security Program rule under the Defense Production Act. Jerusalem Post reported Myanmar disguised Iranian jet fuel as South African diesel to evade US sanctions, and a Tennessee man was sentenced to 17 years for attempting to support Hezbollah.

threads.label: Iran domestic economic and security messaging
threads.summary: IRIB carried government messaging on inflation, wheat prices, subsidies, and Tehran Prosecutor Salehi stating over 10 billion euros in foreign exchange obligations fulfilled with 61 arrests. Defa Press covered the burial of 18-year-old "security martyr" Mohammad Reza Talebi, and Iran International reported comedian Saeed Shakiba indicted for allegedly supporting Israel and the Pahlavi dynasty.

events.title_en: Explosion and fire in a residential building on Ayat Street due to gas leak. Tehran Fire Service Spokesman: At 12:10 noon today, an explosion leading to a fire occurred in a four-storey residential building on Ayat Street, after the intersection of Padarkashani Street. The fourth floor of the building was damaged by an explosion and parts of the surrounding walls were demolished, and three vehicles below the building were damaged. The building was unoccupied and fortunately there were no casualties or injuries. Based on investigations, it is suspected that a gas leak from one of the gas-burning appliances due to negligence and creation of a spark caused the explosion.

events.title: Outbound Investment Security Program Regulations
events.summary: This proposed rule sets forth regulations that would implement Subtitle C of the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, which is codified at Title VIII of the Defense Production Act. The proposed rule would require United States persons to provide notification to the U.S. Department of the Treasury regarding certain transactions involving foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies; and prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies. Where consistent with Title VIII, the proposed rule incorporates certain definitions and concepts from the current regulations governing the Outbound Investment Security Program. The proposed rule also would add applicability dates to the regulations, such that those regulations would continue to apply to activities that occurred within the relevant timeframe.
